sentences.text: Rhynchaeites mcfaddeni is a species within the genus Rhynchaeites, an extinct group of wading birds. Scientists classify this genus as a stem-group threshkiornithid, placing it in the family Threskiornithidae and the subfamily Rhynchaeitinae.

The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of an articulated partial skeleton featuring a sharply tapering beak tip. This shape suggests the bird may have foraged by prying mollusks from their shells.
Ksepka and colleagues described Rhynchaeites mcfaddeni in 2026 based on a largely complete, articulated specimen.
This fossil was found in the United States, specifically in the region of Wyoming, within the Green River Formation.
Researchers suggest Rhynchaeites mcfaddeni likely had divergent foraging strategies from R. messelensis, possibly feeding in streams rather than near lake margins.
It is debated whether the parrot relative Mopsitta tanta is actually a member of the genus Rhynchaeites.
